title: TF2 league matches with RGL ban labels
question: Among RGL accounts fpsdet could compare, how often did each detector fire on cheating-ban labelled accounts against never-banned ones?

origins.name: logs.tf
origins.content: match logs that TF2 community servers upload: each player's shots and hits per weapon, sniper headshots, and kills per minute

origins.name: RGL
origins.content: the competitive league's public ban list, with a reason for each ban

source.mutable: RGL's ban list grows and its reasons can be edited, and a player's logs.tf match list grows with every match, so a later fetch selects different matches; an uploaded log does not change. prepare reports a different download as INPUT_CHANGED.

identity.what: the ban list, the matches chosen for each labelled account and each extra honest player, and every downloaded log

license.terms: Neither site publishes terms for its data. logs.tf's robots.txt asks crawlers to stay off its API, so the fetcher asks for a bounded sample, one or two requests at a time with a pause after each, names this project in its User-Agent, and caches every response.
license.committed: Nothing downloaded is committed: no log, ban, SteamID, name or match id. Only pseudonymous per-player evaluation rows and aggregate numbers are.
license.attribution: Data: logs.tf match logs and RGL's public bans. Not affiliated with Valve, logs.tf or RGL.

pseudonymization.method: Each SteamID becomes tf- and the first 10 hex digits of its HMAC-SHA256 under a 32-byte key the converter creates on the curator's machine (pseudonym.key). The key never leaves it, so published results name nobody. A rebuild with another key gets other ids, and another half of the never-banned players builds the baseline; the key commitment below lets it say so exactly.

label_semantics.statement: RGL's bans are labels, not ground truth: a cheating ban is a league decision about an account, not proof of cheating in any scored match, and never-banned is not proven honest.

acquisition.rate_limit: a 0.6 s pause after each request, at most two in flight, and every response cached
acquisition.note: The published run fetched 20 matches per labelled account. The fetcher's default is 40, which the README's command used to rely on; the benchmark passes 20 explicitly.

rules: Labelled accounts: RGL accounts banned for cheating (not for assisting, distributing or developing cheats) with at least 20 team matches on logs.tf before the ban; their 20 latest team matches before the ban.
Comparison: everyone in those lobbies RGL never banned, with at least 8 matches in the fetched logs, plus 150 never-banned players per half with their own 20 latest team matches.
Equal evidence: every player keeps at most their 20 latest matches; a banned account's only before its ban.
A team match has 12 or more players. Only aimed, hitscan weapons are converted.
A fixed bit of each pseudonym sends never-banned players to the baseline or to be scored, so nobody is judged against a baseline that includes them.
